units.translation: 612 ⟦1⟧ cannot be construed, whereas it stands correctly at 615; ⟦2⟧ . . ⟦3⟧ can be said just as well as ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧ (since ⟦6⟧ = ⟦7⟧, 752. 359 etc.), and because of ⟦8⟧ preceding, an adverb could easily be set. ⟦9⟧ again presupposes Orestes as the defender; in fact, however, he now says nothing more until 744. 614-673 Defense by Apollo, with interjections from the Erinyes. Apollo is thus now really an advocate and behaves somewhat as such a one behaved. Did the role of exegete, which Orestes just assigned to the god, seem to A. too lofty even for tragedy? We would rather say this: Apollo would then have had to teach why this murder was just, and (what is the same thing) why he had commanded it to Orestes, and which murder is just at all and which not; but then the matter was actually decided by an infallible mouth, and no longer a legal dispute, for which judge could have rebelled against it? But the result was to come out differently: equal number of votes against equal, and as the myth is, gods stood against gods; so instead of the exegete, the advocate now speaks, heightening and appealing to the feelings more than clarifying the question, and finally even remarkably sophistically. He speaks four times, at considerable length; the interjections of the chorus comprise only 3, 4 and 5 verses.

The first two verses are the proem for everything. He wants to speak justly, as is fitting before such a court (⟦1⟧ on 571), and to say nothing false, which as a seer he may not. Now he traces with all emphasis all his oracles back to Zeus (on 19), without further expressly testifying that he gave this to Orestes (⟦2⟧ 576, ⟦3⟧ 609; cf. ⟦4⟧ 594, and what Ap. already said at 579f.); thereby he gives his pronouncements the highest conceivable authority, but - on the opposite side stand still older deities.
For ⟦1⟧ the correct change is ⟦2⟧ (Hermann), Kühner-Gerth Synt. II, 427 f.

620 ⟦1⟧ (⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧; as Soph. and Eurip., ⟦5⟧) is otherwise as in Homer, "(to) indicate", here synonymous with ⟦6⟧, and also constructed so. ⟦7⟧ is attested in A. only here (in ⟦8⟧ in a lyric passage); also of the 1st person only the dative ⟦9⟧ ⟦10⟧ occurs in a dochmiac verse (⟦11⟧. 100).
